scope: Canonical full-clear encounter order from the first trainer battle through the current authored frontier. This frontier grows continuously until every campaign, optional, rematch, boss, and postgame trainer encounter in the 810-definition guide is assigned exactly once.
ordering_rule: Use the earliest natural first-playthrough path. Optional trainers are never dropped. Mutually exclusive gender, starter, or partner branches of one physical encounter are grouped under one battle index. Where open terrain or an open side route permits reversal, one order is selected and the ambiguity is documented. Rustboro Gym is canonicalized before the already-accessible Route 116 so each cap-relative encounter has one authored first-reach state.

Second canonical Seashore House challenge. The room permits a different player-selected order, but all three independent trainer flags feed one retry-safe completion callback.
Third canonical Seashore House challenge and final contributor to the shared completion flag. The owner awards six Soda Pops only after Dwayne, Johanna, and Simon have all been defeated.

First mandatory museum ambush after delivering the Devon Goods to Captain Stern. This no-intro battle begins a three-fight scripted Aqua sequence; the player receives no automatic healing before the second Grunt.
Second mandatory Grunt attacks immediately after the first Grunt's defeat dialogue and movement, with no party heal or normal preparation window between the two battles.

Archie enters after both Grunts. The native script explicitly heals the player's party before this boss battle, so Archie is designed as a fresh maximum-difficulty fight rather than the third leg of the Grunt attrition check.

First trainer encounter after the Museum clears Route 110. Isabel at (10,76) and Kaleb at (7,76) have intersecting two-tile sight lines across the only ground corridor, producing a native 3+3 two-opponent double when the player has at least two usable Pokémon. Each source record remains independently reachable if the other has already been defeated.

First Puzzle 1 trainer after the Route 110 pair. Sally is always first and geometrically unavoidable during a normal completion: her six-tile sight line crosses the only route out of the entrance region. Her defeat flag is not checked by the scroll, door, or Mental Herb reward.

Required within optional Puzzle 1 by current collision geometry, but not by a script flag. Eddie's two-tile sight line crosses every exit approach. Eddie and Robin may be fought in either order after Sally; Eddie is the canonical guide tie-break only.

Required within optional Puzzle 1 by current collision geometry, but not by a script flag. Robin's two-tile sight line crosses every scroll approach. Robin and Eddie may be fought in either order after Sally; the Mental Herb reward itself depends only on puzzle state.
Optional eastern Route 110 detour near the Trick House latitude. It may be cleared before or after Puzzle 1; puzzle-first is the canonical full-clear choice.

Mandatory three-tile coordinate-triggered rival milestone before Mauville. Player gender and starter element choose one of six records, while source slot three dynamically becomes the same-generation middle counter-starter across all seven supported trios. Loss cleanly retriggers state 0; victory awards the Itemfinder and keeps the cap at 30.

Ground-road Edwin at (34,40) faces right four tiles and Joseph at (36,40) faces left three tiles; their shared trigger at (35,40) creates a native 3+3 pair when both are undefeated and the player has two usable Pokémon. Either surviving trainer remains independently fightable. Edwin owns the Match Call chain; Joseph has no rematch or item reward.

Edward at (3,39) and Alyssa at (10,39) face each other across the six-tile corridor, producing a deterministic native pair when entered between them. Either can run independently if the other is already defeated or the player has only one usable Pokémon. Neither owns a rematch or scripted reward.
Optional ground-road detour at (10,19), facing down one tile. Dale uses one independent trainer script and has no rematch, callback, or item reward.
Optional northern ground-road detour at (33,15), facing left one tile. Jaclyn follows Dale in the south-to-north full-clear order and has no rematch, callback, or item reward.

First canonical Cycling Road clear after obtaining a Bike in Mauville. Anthony patrols x=9-19 across y=30-31 with three-tile sight. His live sight region never intersects Abigail's fixed westward line, so he is an independent optional single with no callback, Match Call chain, scripted reward, or native-pair branch.

Independent fixed Cycling Road trainer at (30,31), facing left four tiles. Her sight region x=26-29 never intersects Anthony's patrol, so no joint branch exists. Abigail alone owns the Match Call registration and later rematch chain; the first encounter remains an ordinary single.
Moving Cycling Road trainer centered at (16,55) with three-tile sight. Benjamin owns a Match Call rematch chain but no direct item reward.
Moving Cycling Road trainer centered at (16,73) with a long vertical route and three-tile sight. Jasmine has no rematch, callback, or direct item reward.

Southern moving Cycling Road trainer centered at (21,78) with two-tile sight. Jacob has no rematch or direct item reward. Cycling course rating independently awards Electric Seed or Quick Claw and is not gated by trainer victories.

Script-driven Wally scene at the Mauville Gym doorway. The player may initially decline and a loss remains retryable; an explicit two-usable-Pokémon guard now protects the no-intro double. Victory sets FLAG_DEFEATED_WALLY_MAUVILLE, moves Wally and his uncle, enables the later call, and physically clears the Gym entrance. No item reward or automatic cap change occurs.

Vivian at (1,16) faces up two tiles and Kirk at (1,13) faces down two tiles; both see (1,14) and (1,15). Crossing the shared lane with two usable Pokémon and both undefeated creates a native 3+3 joint double, while side lanes or manual engagement allow either independent four-member single. Both trainer records intentionally remain single so the one-usable fallback is safe. They are globally optional and own no callback, rematch, or reward.

Ben at (5,10) faces left across the center choke. He is unavoidable on the Switch-3 solution but globally optional because the Switch-4 right route bypasses him. His independent trainer record is a four-member double with no callback, rematch, or reward.

Shawn at (7,8) faces down one tile and Angelo at (7,10) faces up one tile; both see exactly (7,9). The Switch-4 right route creates a native 3+3 joint double when both are undefeated and the player has two usable Pokémon, while manual engagement permits either independent four-member single. Both trainer records intentionally remain single so the one-usable fallback is safe. Ben's route bypasses both. Neither owns a callback, rematch, or reward.

Fixed six-member double after either valid barrier route. Victory grants the Dynamo Badge, raises the strict cap from 30 to 40, enables Rock Smash field use, preserves the native Raichu and Wattson registrations, and gives Wise Glasses through legacy Volt Switch-named script labels. There is no scripted post-battle heal; the Gym Guide's separate twelve Moomoo Milks are not a trainer reward.

Because the route is physically open earlier, both Anna and Meg now truthfully wait for the Dynamo Badge before loading the fixed cap-40 endpoint roster. Anna at (42,6) and Meg at (43,6) are two overworld avatars for one trainer definition, not two native opponents. Either script starts the same guarded four-member solo double and registers the same Match Call/rematch chain.

Fixed lower-lane trainer at (33,11), alternating up/right with four-tile sight. Isaac now truthfully waits for the Dynamo Badge, then both his first fight and Match Call rematches use guarded native doubles without changing his ownership chain. Isaac and Dylan remain reversible in open terrain; Isaac is the canonical lower-lane-first tie-break.

Horizontal patrol from (38,16) with range eight and four-tile sight. Dylan now truthfully waits for the Dynamo Badge, then both his first fight and Match Call rematches use guarded native doubles. The tier-2 rematch receives a distinct fourth placeholder so every reachable rematch tier remains an even double; their full team redesign remains separately indexed debt.

Maria wanders around (26,13) in a two-by-two range with five-tile sight. She now truthfully waits for the Dynamo Badge and remains an intentional four-member single as a format break after three consecutive Route 117 doubles. All four Match Call records are single-format; tiers 2-4 remain separately indexed team-design debt.

Fixed at (17,12), facing up with four-tile sight. Derek is a normal independent single with no callback, direct reward, Match Call registration, or rematch. Derek and the upper-meadow cluster are reversible in open terrain; the lower-lane sweep is the canonical tie-break.

One upper-meadow formation dossier must cover every real branch. Aisha at (21,4) faces west four tiles; moving Melina begins at (16,4) and can face east; Brandi at (15,4) faces east four tiles. Approach and patrol timing can create Aisha+Melina or Brandi+Melina native doubles, leave the third trainer for a later single, or permit manual split singles. All three records remain independently source-owned and none has a callback, reward, or rematch.

Lydia rotates counterclockwise at (8,10) with three-tile sight. Her six-member record is double while the current first-fight and rematch opcodes are single, so source closure must add the usable-party guard while preserving Lydia's independent Match Call chain and lack of direct item reward.

entries.category: optional single on deferred east side
entries.access_note: The Verdanturf-side warp reaches Mike at (32,13), facing left with three-tile sight. He is the ordinary three-member single deliberately deferred after Battle 27 and owns no callback, item, or rematch. The farther-west Rock Smash reunion, HM04 Strength gift, and permanent tunnel opening are separate non-battle progression and not Mike's reward. Route 111 south follows this westward detour in the canonical full-clear sequence.

Route 111 south follows the Rusturf detour. Victor stands at (13,114) outside the family house with talk-only trigger; accepting Route111_Text_BattleOurFamily starts four consecutive trainerbattle_no_intro battles with no healing between them. The whole gauntlet waits for Badge 3 behind one family-level guard so cap-40 levels stay truthful.

Victoria exits the house immediately after Victor's defeat inside the same scripted sequence. The player cannot heal, shop, or save-menu between legs, so her attrition garden is budgeted against a party already damaged by Victor.
Vivi exits the house immediately after Victoria inside the same scripted sequence. Her prodigy team is the gauntlet's offense spike and precedes Vicky's single ace with no healing between.

Vicky is the fourth consecutive no-intro battle and the gauntlet's single-ace finale. Her lone No Guard Machamp at cap+3 closes the family exam against whatever the player has left; the Winstrate house rest follows only after her defeat.

Walking the west desert-fence path north from the family house, Irene at (10,82) faces left and right with two-tile sight before Travis at (11,71). She is an independent three-member single with no callback, reward, or rematch, gated on Badge 3.

Travis at (11,71) faces down, left, and right with three-tile sight just north of Irene. His four-member record is a usable-party-guarded double with no callback, reward, or rematch, gated on Badge 3. Gabby and Ty's shared global interview records remain unresolved-chapter work, and the desert interior stays sealed behind the Go-Goggles, so Route 112 south continues the canonical clear.
Route 112 south is the next stop on the canonical clear after the Route 111 west path. Hiker Brice guards the Fiery Path trailhead; Trent follows him before the Mt. Chimney cable car story block.
Trent is the second Route 112 hiker and owns a Match Call rematch family; his tier-1 record is the authored target and his rematch rosters remain later design debt.

After Brice and Trent, the canonical full-clear Route 112 south loop takes the remaining fixed Camper Larry at (29,49), facing down with three-tile sight. Carol follows as the remaining moving south-loop trainer before Fiery Path; Larry has no Match Call family or direct item reward.

Carol is the remaining south-loop Route 112 trainer after Larry, rotating counterclockwise from (22,46) with three-tile sight. Her two-member independent single precedes entry into Fiery Path in the canonical full clear and owns no callback, rematch family, or direct item reward.

After Fiery Path's north exit, Bryant at (31,7) faces down/right and Shayla at (31,11) faces up/left across the same three-tile vertical lane. Facing/timing can create a native two-opponent double or independent split singles. One dossier must cover every joint/split branch before Route 113.

Route 112's north connection places the player near Route 113 x=90. Before Jaylen, buried Lung at (71,2), left-facing Wyatt at (75,3), and up-facing Lawrence at (71,4) can all detect the player on (71,3). Object order produces Lung+Wyatt first when all are unbeaten; prior flags or direct approaches also expose Lung+Lawrence, Wyatt+Lawrence, and all three split singles. One dossier must close every reachable pair and split before westbound Jaylen.

After resolving the Lung/Wyatt/Lawrence east cluster, Jaylen is the next westbound trainer: a stationary Youngster at (62,8), facing down with three-tile sight. His source record forces a four-member double and precedes Madeline's moving sight lane.

entries.category: optional moving ash-field Parasol Lady encounter

Tori and Tia are the next westbound physical encounter after Madeline: adjacent twin objects at (45,6) and (46,6), both facing down with one-tile sight and both invoking the same guarded TRAINER_TORI_AND_TIA record. One dossier must verify both object scripts and shared dialogue paths.

Dillon is the next westbound physical encounter after buried Lao: a Youngster at (21,11), facing down/left with three-tile sight. His source record forces a four-member double but the map script is currently a single opcode, so Battle 93 must verify and repair the one-Pokemon guard path.

Sophie at (7,6) walks down/up and Coby at (7,13) walks up/down along the same west-edge vertical lane; both have six-tile sight and three-tile movement ranges. Timing exposes a native two-opponent double or either split single. One dossier must close every branch before Fallarbor Town.

After Fallarbor, Nolan is the eastern Route 114 Fisherman at (25,6). His sight range is zero, so he is a direct-interaction optional encounter near the entrance/pond rather than a forced sight battle. His source record forces a double; Battle 95 must verify the script's two-Pokemon guard before the southbound lane.

Kai at (28,16) faces down/left with three-tile sight and Charlotte at (28,20) faces up with three-tile sight across the same east-pond vertical lane. Facing/timing and prior flags expose a native pair or either split single. One dossier must close every branch before the southbound Route 114 trainers.
Claude stands at (19,26) with sight range zero immediately south-west of the Kai/Charlotte pond lane. He is the next north-to-south optional encounter before Nancy and the Tyra/Ivy pair.
Nancy moves and looks around at (19,35) with three-tile sight on the main north-to-south path below Claude. She is the next physical encounter before the Tyra/Ivy sight pair.

Tyra at (23,44) and Ivy at (24,44) each face down with one-tile sight and both invoke the same guarded TRAINER_TYRA_AND_IVY double. The two object scripts are one physical encounter, not split trainer records.
Shane faces right at (22,50) with three-tile sight on the main path immediately below Tyra and Ivy. He is the next north-to-south physical encounter before Steve and Bernie.
